I've been farming this land for 35 years and I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent, the well gives me water when I need it, and the wheat-maize rotation is what everyone around here does — and for good reason. My kids and daughter-in-law bring in some cash from factory work in the city, so I'm not desperate, but I still need the farm to produce well. Eight mouths is eight mouths.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant all 20 mu to wheat in October after the maize comes off. I'll buy the improved variety the county extension recommends — not the cheapest seed, but not the fancy expensive stuff either. I've used Shi4185 type varieties for years and they do fine. I'll do rotary tillage after I clear the maize straw — it breaks up the soil nicely. I split my nitrogen: some base fertilizer mixed with phosphorus and potassium before planting, then urea top-dress at jointing in April. I'll irrigate three times: once in late November before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide passes — a winter herbicide and a spring spray for aphids and powdery mildew. I expect around 450 kg/mu, which is normal for here.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I'll direct seed maize without tilling — saves time and fuel, and the wheat stubble mulches the soil a bit. I've been doing this for about 8 years now and yields haven't dropped. I use a popular hybrid — something like Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed dealer has that's similar and proven locally. Summer rain usually handles most of the water needs, but I'll irrigate once at planting if it's dry, which it often is in June. I'll spray herbicide early, and I'll watch for corn borer — one more spray if I see damage. Nitrogen goes on in two hits: some at planting, the rest as big bell stage. I expect around 550 kg/mu.
